sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4 million in FY2016 to $14,342.9 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was two step changes rather than a smooth climb: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 and then fell 24.3% in FY2022 [D241][D292].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of the 89.1% growth in FY2021, on $5,828.0 million of US sales [D582][D241][S48].
Operating margin peaked at 55.7% in FY2021 and has fallen every year since, to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30].
In FY2025 revenue grew only 1.0%, with net product sales down 17.3% (a 9.3pp drag) offset by collaboration revenue up 21.0% (+9.0pp) [D440][D506][D507][D522][D523].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% and subtracted 14.2pp from growth on lower volumes and a lower net selling price [D577][D578][P10].
The offset was Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits, up 33.6% and worth 9.3pp, driven by higher Dupixent sales [D591][D592][P9].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 5.4%, so operating income fell 10.3% [D464][D457][D441].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% against net income growth of 2.1% as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D444][D442][D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the 55.7% high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off the margin and SG&A added 2.0pp back, leaving the 3.2pp net decline [D465][D466][D453].
SG&A fell 8.6% mainly on lower charitable contributions to Good Days [D456][P5].
In FY2025 net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin, as other income of $1,652.8 million and a 13.9% tax rate lifted the bottom line [F50][F30][D797][X117][D427].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9 million was 1.11x net income in FY2025, against a 1.10x window median [F80][F40][D428][D787].
Free cash flow of $4,080.5 million was a 28.4% margin, above the 26.4% median but below the 40.6% FY2021 high [F100][D425][D757][D756].
Capex of $898.4 million was 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [F90][D424][D430].
Stock-based compensation of $993.7 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash reached $16,879.9 million, or 117.7% of revenue, against a peer median of -50.7% (n=8) [D434][D435][D781].
That ranks at the 100th percentile of the peer group, with debt flat at $1,985.9 million [D780][D433].
Buybacks of $3,438.6 million plus dividends of $370.3 million absorbed 93.3% of free cash flow [X137][X140][D437].
The balance sheet is the strongest part of the story, and the FY2025 buyback is what produced the 5.6% share-count decline [D459].
Operating margin has fallen four straight years, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp slide [F26][F27][F28][F29][F30][R1].
The decline is now driven by EYLEA erosion rather than one-off charges, so the margin base looks structurally lower [R1].
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table are later recasts: $5,145.6 million versus $6,710.8 million as first reported, and $6,557.6 million versus $7,863.4 million [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so I have not built conclusions on the FY2018-FY2019 comparisons [R2].
Whether US EYLEA sales, $2,747.8 million in FY2025, fall further or stabilize will show in the FY2026 10-K [S43].
Whether the operating margin holds above the 24.9% FY2025 low or extends the four-year decline will show in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D749].
Whether R&D stays near 40.8% of revenue, versus the 34.6% median, will show in the FY2026 10-K [D420][D760].
